best_for: Backend developers who poke at Postgres, MySQL and Redis every day and would rather pay once for a native client than run a heavy IDE.

points.title: One app, many databases
points.text: It connects to PostgreSQL, MySQL, MariaDB, SQL Server, SQLite, Oracle, Redshift, Snowflake, BigQuery, ClickHouse and DuckDB, plus Redis, MongoDB, Cassandra, Elasticsearch and DynamoDB.

points.title: Review before you write
points.text: Edits to rows and table structure stay pending until you review the generated statements and commit. Safe mode can ask for confirmation before any query runs, which helps on production.

points.title: Free trial with tight limits
points.text: Without a license you get two tabs, two windows and two advanced filters at a time. Filters are not in the free Windows version at all, and TablePlus says limits may change.

points.title: Pay once, renew for updates
points.text: Basic is $99 for one desktop seat, Standard is $129 for two, and Team is $79 per seat with a three-seat minimum. Each includes a year of updates; after that the app keeps working, and renewal is $59 per device. Prices were read on the date below.

points.title: Your data stays direct
points.text: Connections go from your machine to the database, over SSH or SSL/TLS if you choose, and TablePlus says data never passes through its servers.

points.title: Mac needs 12 or later
points.text: The Mac app is a universal build for Intel and Apple Silicon on macOS 12 or later. Windows needs .NET 4.8 and installs for all users. The Windows listing keeps 85 versions; macOS lists only the current release.
